draft.title: The equilibrium constant
card: The equilibrium constant, K, compares the amounts of products and reactants at equilibrium. It is worked out from concentrations in mol/L, shown in square brackets.
For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, K = [C]^c [D]^d ÷ ([A]^a [B]^b). Products go on top, reactants on the bottom, and each concentration is raised to the power of its coefficient.
Only gases and aqueous species go in the expression. Pure solids and pure liquids are left out.
A large K means products are favoured, so the equilibrium mixture contains mostly products. A small K means reactants are favoured.
draft.remember: K = products over reactants, each to the power of its coefficient. Large K, products favoured.

a.q: Which is the correct equilibrium expression for N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g)?
a.why: Products go on top and reactants on the bottom, and each concentration is raised to the power of its coefficient. The second option is upside down, so it would give the reverse reaction.
a.clue: Coefficients become powers, and products go on top.

b.q: At a set temperature, the reaction 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g) has K = 3 × 10^24. What does this say about the equilibrium mixture?
opts: It contains mostly SO3, so products are favoured
It contains mostly SO2 and O2, so reactants are favoured
It contains about equal amounts of reactants and products
It is reached very slowly because K is so large
b.why: A very large K means the product concentration is much greater than the reactant concentrations at equilibrium, so products are favoured. K compares amounts at equilibrium. It does not tell you how fast equilibrium is reached.
b.clue: K is products over reactants. What does a huge ratio mean?

b.best: It contains mostly SO3, so products are favoured

problems.detail: Why (a) refers to 'the second option' as the upside-down expression. Options are shown in a random order, so this position reference can point students to the wrong option. It should name the expression instead: K = [N2][H2]^3 ÷ [NH3]^2.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear answer. The only issue is that Why (a) calls the upside-down expression 'the second option', which will be wrong when the options are shuffled.
